text: >>18568486 Two german examples from the Napoleonic Wars are Eleonore Prochaska and Friederike Krüger. Prochaska disguised herself as a men and joined the Lützow Freikorps in June of 1813. In September 1813 she fought at the Battle of the Göhrde and was wounded there by cannister shot. This led to her "discovery" - three weeks later she died. Krüger joined the Colberg Grenadier Regiment in 1813 also disguised as a men. She was soon discovered but had served with such distinction that King Friedrich Wilhelm III. of Prussia allowed her to stay in the army and serve openly as a women. At the Battle of Dennewitz in September 1813 she was wounded and due to her bravery promoted to an NCO and got awarded the Iron Cross 2nd Class. She was active for the remainder of the wars and got honorably discharged in late 1815. The prussian king even paid for her dowry for her 1816 marriage. Pic rel is her grave
